items.title: Tata Sons board meet postponed to Nov 30 after Noel raises concerns
items.rss_summary: Tata Sons on Monday postponed a crucial board meeting which was set to discuss the way ahead on the listing of the holding company of the country's largest conglomerate by four days to November 30. The postponement has been necessitated after a letter from Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata on Sunday raising concerns about the mandatory seven-day notice period for a board meeting not being followed, as the agenda was put up only four days in advance. The agenda for the meeting has not been changed, and it is only the day which has been postponed to November 30 from November 26 earlier to give sufficient time for all the directors to prepare for the meeting, as per people in the know. The crucial meeting on November 30 will discuss items including RBI-mandated listing of Tata Sons or ways ahead on complying with the central bank's requests, they said. Divisions among the top echelons on the way ahead for the group had come into the open at the last board meet of Tata Sons on September 1

items.title: India's gold imports fall 40% to $24.7 billion in April-October 2026: CTI
items.rss_summary: Gold imports into India declined by around 40 per cent in April-October this year compared to the corresponding period last year, with the country purchasing gold worth USD 24.7 billion during the seven months, Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) Chairman Brijesh Goyal said on Monday. According to Goyal, India imported gold worth USD 41.24 billion between April and October 2025, while the figure stood at USD 24.7 billion during the same period this year, marking a decline of USD 16.46 billion. He said the figures reflected a significant reduction in gold purchases during the current financial year. Gold imports in the 2025-26 financial year stood at around USD 72 billion, while the purchases for 2026-27 are estimated to be between USD 35 billion and USD 40 billion, he said. Goyal attributed the decline in gold purchases to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal, saying the reduction was visible in the trade figures.
